summary: P0 atomic counter fix verified end-to-end. 13/13 new tests pass + 9/9 iteration-5 regression tests pass = 22/22 total. Covered: POST without order_number increments by 1; POST with higher order_number jumps the counter; POST with lower/already-used order_number returns counter+1 (KEY DUPLICATE-NUMBER FIX); POST with equal order_number returns counter+1; 10 parallel POSTs without explicit number produce 10 unique sequential numbers; 10 parallel POSTs all requesting order_number=100 produce 10 unique numbers (100..109) thanks to atomic $max in find_one_and_update; GET /api/orders/next-number returns counter+1 (1 initially, 4 after 3 creates, requires auth); UNIQUE index (restaurant_id, order_number) is created at startup and direct duplicate insert in MongoDB raises DuplicateKeyError; regressions intact (DELETE never lowers counter; GET /api/orders defaults to pending).
critical_code_review_comments: create_order (server.py L651-714) now uses an aggregation pipeline in find_one_and_update with $max(counter+1, requested). This is correctly atomic at the document level: motor/MongoDB serializes concurrent updates on the same restaurant doc, so the counter is monotonic and no two concurrent POSTs can ever read the same post-update value. Verified with 10 parallel POSTs (no duplicates) and 10 parallel POSTs with the same explicit order_number=100 (got 100..109).
GET /api/orders/next-number (L731-743) reads order_counter directly from the DB and returns counter+1. Verified to require auth (401/403 without token).

Unique index on (restaurant_id, order_number) (server.py L2492-2499) is created on startup; verified present via index_information() and verified to actually reject duplicate inserts with DuplicateKeyError. Note: index creation is wrapped in try/except so existing duplicates at boot only log a warning and do not crash startup - acceptable for migration safety.

MINOR/COSMETIC: server.py L2472/L2476 still uses deprecated @app.on_event("startup")/("shutdown"); same DeprecationWarning observed in iteration_5. Recommend migrating to FastAPI lifespan handlers when convenient.

MINOR: create_order's aggregation pipeline coerces requested via `data.order_number or 0`. If a client deliberately sends order_number=0 or negative, $max(counter+1, <=0) collapses to counter+1, which is the safe behavior. Pydantic does not constrain to >0 - consider adding `Field(gt=0)` if you want explicit 422 instead of silent fallback. Non-blocking.

MINOR: Backup file write to backup_flaminio.txt (L703-706) happens AFTER counter increment. If the disk write fails the order is still committed to DB and counter advanced, which is the correct precedence. Just noting.

OBSERVATION: The unique index protects only the active `orders` collection. After midnight_reset clears the collection, the next day starts fresh. archived_orders has no uniqueness constraint - acceptable since archives accumulate across days and order_number resets to 0 each day.

rca_of_the_issue: ROOT CAUSE: pre-fix create_order had two separate code paths: (a) when client did NOT pass order_number, an atomic $inc on order_counter was used; (b) when client DID pass order_number, an `update_one` set order_counter to MAX(current, requested) WITHOUT being atomic with the subsequent insert. Two concurrent clients passing the same number could both read counter=N, both call update_one to N, and both insert with order_number=N -> duplicates. Additionally the frontend Cassa computed the next number from in-memory `pending` orders, which is a subset that empties as soon as orders are completed, so on a busy night the frontend would propose numbers that had already been issued and archived. FIX: (1) Single atomic aggregation-pipeline find_one_and_update with $max([counter+1, requested]) - guarantees monotonicity even if client sends a stale/duplicate number. (2) New GET /api/orders/next-number endpoint that returns the authoritative counter+1 from the DB, used by the Cassa frontend instead of computing from local pending list. (3) UNIQUE index (restaurant_id, order_number) on the active orders collection as last-line-of-defense against any remaining race or buggy direct insert. VERIFIED via tests: requested=5 with counter=10 returns 11 (not 5); 10 parallel POSTs with same order_number=100 yield 100..109 all unique; direct duplicate insert raises DuplicateKeyError; next-number returns counter+1.
